stem: A 9-year-old has had an angry and irritable mood, frequent arguments with adults, active defiance of rules, and spiteful behavior for 7 months, causing problems at home and school. There is no pattern of severe rights violations or serious rule-breaking behavior. Which disorder is most consistent with these findings?

options.D: Adjustment disorder with disturbance of conduct

rationale: Oppositional defiant disorder is characterized by a persistent pattern of angry/irritable mood, argumentative/defiant behavior, or vindictiveness lasting at least 6 months and causing distress or functional impairment. Conduct disorder involves more severe violations of others' rights or major rules. Disruptive mood dysregulation disorder requires a different pattern centered on severe recurrent temper outbursts with persistent irritability over at least 12 months. Therefore B is the best answer.
educational_objective: Differentiate oppositional defiant disorder from conduct disorder and other childhood behavioral disorders using duration, symptom pattern, functional impact, and severity.
source_locator: NCBI Bookshelf ID NBK557443 — Introduction/DSM-5-TR diagnostic criteria; Differential Diagnosis — Conduct Disorder and Disruptive Mood Dysregulation Disorder
source_claim_supported: ODD involves angry/irritable mood, argumentative/defiant behavior or vindictiveness for at least 6 months with impairment; conduct disorder is distinguished by more severe rights/rule violations; DMDD has a distinct severe-outburst and persistent-irritability pattern lasting at least 12 months.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity — mental health concepts and behavioral/emotional disorders
blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — childhood disruptive behavior disorders
correction_summary: Rewrote the stem as a concise age-specific vignette with functional impairment and an explicit severity distinction; replaced weak distractors with conduct disorder, DMDD and adjustment disorder; retained B as uniquely correct; reduced difficulty from hard to easy because the final item is direct diagnostic-pattern recognition.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Child/adolescent mental health — disruptive behavior disorders
audit_findings.currentness: NCBI chapter last updated October 29, 2024 and listed in the 2026 StatPearls edition.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Duration, symptom domains, impairment requirement and key differential distinctions are supported by the cited chapter.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: The vignette supplies more than 6 months of ODD-domain symptoms and excludes the severity pattern expected for conduct disorder; DMDD and adjustment disorder lack defining features. B is uniquely defensible.
audit_findings.cueing: All answer choices are diagnostic labels of comparable form.
audit_findings.blueprint: Psychosocial Integrity is appropriate for recognition of behavioral/emotional disorders in a child.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read the final stem/options without reference to the key and confirmed no second answer remained.
